raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through the way I always do at the start of the season.

---

I'm 57, been working these 5 mu my whole adult life. Wheat and maize, same as my father did, same as most folks in the village. My wife helps in the busy times, my oldest son works construction in Handan so he sends money but can't help with the fields much. Two grandkids in school. With only 5 mu we can't live off farming alone — that off-farm money is what keeps us going. So my job with the land is: don't mess it up, get a steady harvest, don't waste money on fancy things.

**Wheat (winter):** I'll plant around October 10-15, same as always, after the maize comes off in early October. I use the local improved variety the seed shop sells — I think it's Jimai 22 or something like that, the shopkeeper tells me what's good. I buy fresh seed, don't save my own anymore, it's not worth the trouble for 5 mu.

For fertilizer, the extension guy came through a couple years back and said 15 kg N per mu is enough, but honestly I put down a bit more — maybe 18 kg N total. I do a compound fertilizer (something like 15-15-15) before planting, about 40 kg per mu, then topdress urea at jointing in March, maybe 15 kg urea per mu. My father always said "yellow wheat means hungry wheat" so I'd rather put a little extra than watch it go pale. I'll irrigate 3 times — before winter to help it root, once at jointing, once at grain fill. Water from our village well isn't free, the electricity bill adds up, but skipping irrigation on wheat is asking for trouble.

Expected yield: around 450 kg/mu if the weather's normal. Last year I got 470, year before 420 because of that dry spell in May.

**Maize (summer):** Right after wheat harvest in mid-June, I've got maybe 5 days to get the maize in. I don't till — nobody does anymore for summer maize, there's no time. I hire the neighbor with the no-till planter, pay him maybe 30 yuan per mu. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop has, costs around 50-60 yuan per mu.

Fertilizer is similar to wheat but a bit less because maize doesn't need as much here — I'll use the compound at planting, around 35 kg per mu, then topdress urea at big flare leaf stage, about 12 kg urea. Total N maybe 15 kg/mu. Irrigation depends on the summer rain — usually I only need to irrigate once or twice, sometimes not at all if the rains come right. Last summer was dry so I pumped twice.

Pesticide — I'll spray herbicide after planting (atrazine mix, standard stuff), and if I see borers in July I'll spray insecticide. Don't overdo it, the chemicals cost money.

Expected maize yield: about 500 kg/mu. Good maize years I've hit 550.

**Cost-wise:** For 5 mu total, I'm probably spending around 600-700 yuan per mu per year across both crops — seed, fertilizer, water/electricity, pesticide, hired planter. That's 3,000-3,500 yuan total. Not counting my own labor. Wheat sells around 2.4 yuan/kg, maize around 2.2. Do the math and you see why my son has to work in the city.
